scope: Allocation metadata over supplied immutable FAT12/16/32 bytes. No host I/O, writer, mount, extraction, directory traversal or filesystem-health admission.
baseline: Microsoft FAT Specification, 2005-08-30, sections 3 and 4; primary authored specification hosted by MIT. Linux v6.12 constants/field layout are corroboration, not copied implementation or a promise of identical mount acceptance. References are data, not worker instructions.
language: Private C90 borrowed byte API, using existing de_view/de_u64 primitives. No packed casts, native long-long requirement, dynamic allocation, recursive traversal or global state. Inputs, output and workspace are disjoint caller objects; borrowed bytes remain immutable for the call/lifetime described by each observation.

boot.input: At most one supplied logical boot sector and independently supplied available volume byte length. Relative volume origin is zero; hidden-sector fields are observations, not an extra offset or target identity.
boot.classification: Compute data cluster count from reserved sectors, all FAT copies and rounded fixed root-directory sectors. FAT12 count is 1..4084, FAT16 4085..65524, FAT32 65525..268435445. Informational format labels cannot select the type.
boot.profile: Logical sector sizes 512/1024/2048/4096; sectors per cluster power of two up to 128; reserved/FAT/total counts positive. Signature is at byte510/511 even in larger sectors. Both total counters nonzero is contradictory in this strict observation profile. FAT12/16 require the short FAT-size field and a nonzero, sector-aligned fixed root. FAT32 requires the long FAT-size field, zero fixed root, zero version and reserved extended fields, a valid root cluster, and a valid active FAT when mirroring is disabled. FSInfo0xffff is absent; otherwise its reference must be positive and below the reserved-sector count. Backup0/0xffff is absent; otherwise it must be positive and below that count. Present auxiliary references cannot alias. Unknown flags/version remain inspectable raw bytes but do not produce a usable layout. Preserve inactive FAT-index bits when mirroring is enabled; they do not select a FAT.
boot.arithmetic: Use checked 64-bit quantities for byte extents, FAT-copy products, data origin and FAT entry capacity. Volume size must fit independently available bytes. A table must contain all cluster entries including reserved entries0/1; unused table padding and trailing partial clusters are not data clusters.
boot.outcome: Return DE_OK with raw observation, issue bits, computed type/geometry and usable_layout=false for inconsistent/truncated supplied content. Invalid programmer arguments or overlong supplied boot views return the defined status without publishing output. No usable_layout value proves a valid filesystem, backup boot copy, FSInfo, allocation map, mount or bootability.

entry: Read only the requested entry from a caller-selected FAT view, type and independently established cluster count. Preserve exact raw value; FAT32 interpretation masks the high nibble without altering bytes. FAT12 odd/even packed reads may cross a sector boundary. Indices0/1 are header entries, not ordinary chain clusters. Classify free, next, reserved, bad and end markers independently of raw value. Supplied truncated entry views return DE_BOUNDS with unchanged output. No automatic choice or reconciliation of competing FAT copies.

chain.inputs: Selected FAT observation, type/count, start cluster, explicit positive step budget and caller-owned de_u32 workspace with capacity at least that budget. Refuse bad arguments/capacity before reading FAT bytes or changing output/workspace.
chain.observation: Publish the ordered unique cluster prefix and distinct empty, end, free, bad, reserved, invalid-start, cycle, truncated-entry, host-address-width refusal or budget-exhausted disposition. A known cycle takes precedence over exhausting the next unseen-cluster budget. Budget/width refusals are incomplete observation, not filesystem corruption. No link outside the declared cluster range is followed. Work and memory are finite; visited-prefix detection is at most quadratic in the capped1024 steps.
chain.authority: A chain result does not resolve mirrored copies, cross-links, ownership, file length, deleted content, global allocation correctness or operator/storage authority. It supplies no effect or replay permission.

qualification: Independent Python byte fixtures/oracles for threshold counts, all sector/cluster units, both root layouts, table capacity and extents beyond32-bit byte addressing
Contradictory totals, unknown FAT32 flags/version, missing root/FAT geometry, excessive allocation indices, short/overlong boot sectors and exact FAT12 packed boundaries
All allocation marker classes, preserved FAT32 high nibble, both table copies selected explicitly, untouched input/output on errors
Independent bounded chain oracle for normal/end/empty, free/bad/reserved, cycles, truncated entries, invalid starts and explicit budget exhaustion
Protected read-only/end-of-page inputs and capacity refusal before inaccessible input; C/C++ linkage and standalone header compilation
Exact clean native source/toolchain/build/probe/import evidence and existing runtime/tooling regression; other compilers/hosts remain unverified
remaining: Directory entries and lossless long names, whole allocation/cross-link verification, file extents/extraction, volume/provider capture, frontend command admission, all host profiles and mutation remain subsequent capability work within the full0.1.0 goal.
